scenario: [LCCO.6.2]: an `on` predicate has a `where` clause's typing rules with `response` bound to the response fact, and the body sees the same fact. So `response.x - response.y` is `Duration - Duration` in both, which [RLOW.6.1.6] lowers through FN_MAX and which is `0_s` when the right operand is the larger ([LTIM.4.1.1]). Rule `plan` calls `svc.read` for a Visit; the host answers on the call's own correlation (`corr_from_call: 0`) with `x` 2 s and `y` 5 s. The predicate `response.x - response.y == 0_s` holds, and the body emits a Gap with `text: (response.x - response.y)::String`; rule `show` logs it. The messages are exactly ['1 0s']. Each wrong reading fails: a predicate lowered with no typing environment is Int `-`, -3 s, which is not `0_s`, so nothing fires; a body lowered so leaves the cast unlowered, so the sibling is skipped and nothing is logged. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete`'s `sibling_rules`, whose `on` arm lowers the predicate and the body with `response` bound (`cx_env`), read by `rlow_6_1_6_saturating` and `cast_fn`.
rules_ds:
schema Reply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    x: Duration
    y: Duration

service svc.read:
    kwarg n: Int
    response Reply

schema Visit scope logical:
    id: Int key

schema Gap scope ttl 1_h:
    id: Int
    text: String

rule plan:
    Visit v
->
    call svc.read n: v.id cooldown: 1_h
        on response.x - response.y == 0_s:
            emit Gap id: v.id text: (response.x - response.y)::String

rule show:
    Gap g
->
    log info "{g.id} {g.text}"
